newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN RUPIAH TUMBLES ON CONTAGION EFFECT.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN RUPIAH TUMBLES ON CONTAGION EFFECT.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah tumbled to 2,646/49 against the dollar at 0145 GMT on Tuesday from an opening of 2,610/20 on falls in the Malaysian ringgit and the Singapore dollar, dealers said.
They said falls in the ringgit and the Singapore dollar spilled over to the rupiah at the opening, driving the rupiah down to a low of 2,655 before it recovered on local dollar selling.
"It's the contagion effect again. The market is a bit nervous, with spreads trending to widen again. But volume was moderate," one foreign bank dealer said.
He said stop-loss limits were triggered after the rupiah fell through the 2,620 level.
The dealer said operators remained nervous and cautious, waiting for further developments on the ringgit and the Singapore dollar.
The Singapore dollar dipped briefly to 1.50 to the U.S. dollar after an official of the country's de-facto central bank said the currency's exchange rate was at an appropriate level.
An official of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said the Singapore dollar's level was appropriate to what was happening in the market.
The official said the U.S. dollar had been rising in currency markets recently and the Singapore dollar had depreciated by about five percent against the U.S. unit since the start of 1997.
Indonesia's central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,588/2,636 on Monday from 2,573/2,621 on Friday.
